children: U.S. private equity firm to acquire 24.9 per cent stake as hospital chain plans to expand capacity to 3,250 beds

U.S.-based private equity firm Advent International will invest Rs 3,150 crore (USD 328.5 million) in Yatharth Hospital & Trauma Care Services for a 24.9 per cent stake, marking a major private equity investment in India's hospital sector as the healthcare provider plans to expand its bed capacity. The transaction was announced on 17 September, 2026.

The investment adds to a series of private equity transactions in India's healthcare sector, as institutional investors continue to deploy capital into hospital networks and specialised healthcare businesses. Yatharth Hospitals, established in 2008, primarily operates in northern India. According to Reuters, the company currently operates nine multispecialty hospitals with around 2,800 operational beds and plans to increase its capacity to 3,250 beds. Following the investment, the founding Tyagi family will remain the company's largest shareholder.

The Rs 3,150 crore investment will give Advent a 24.9 per cent stake in Yatharth Hospitals, while the hospital chain gains institutional capital as it prepares for its next phase of expansion. The transaction also reflects continued private equity activity in India's organised healthcare market. Reuters reported that KKR recently agreed to acquire Swedish healthcare provider Medicover's India business for USD 1.4 billion, while Blackstone acquired a controlling stake in CARE Hospitals in 2023.

BPEA EQT also acquired a majority stake in fertility-services provider Indira IVF in the same year. The Yatharth investment comes as hospital operators expand capacity to meet demand for multispecialty and specialised healthcare services across India's growing urban and regional markets.

Yatharth's planned increase from around 2,800 operational beds to 3,250 beds represents an addition of approximately 450 beds to its existing capacity. The expansion is expected to strengthen the group's hospital network as it continues to operate primarily across northern India.

The deal also gives Advent exposure to India's expanding organised hospital sector through a minority stake in an established healthcare operator. The investment is part of a broader trend of private equity firms backing Indian healthcare providers, with hospitals attracting institutional capital for capacity expansion and growth.
